parent.description:
Parent destination for the new content.

Use { "spaceId": "<numeric-space-id>" } to create at the homepage / sidebar root.
Use { "spaceId": "<numeric-space-id>", "parentContentId": "<numeric-content-id>" }
to create under an existing content item.
Use { "parentContentId": "<numeric-content-id>" } when the parent content ID
should be resolved to its space before creation.
Use { "parentContentUrl": "<confluence-content-url>" } when the parent
content URL should be resolved before creation.

Supported parentContentUrl paths include /pages/{id}, /blog/{id},
/whiteboard/{id}, /database/{id}, and /folder/{id}.

If the destination is described only by space key or title, resolve it first
to one of the supported parent shapes above.

contentType.description:
Type of content to create. One of: page, live_doc, blogpost, whiteboard,
database, embed, smart_link, folder, slide.

title.description: Title for the new content. 1-255 characters.

body.description:
Before composing this body, follow the space-instruction decision rule in the tool
description. Reuse known instruction state and do not repeat the space lookup per write.
Body content. For whiteboard and database it is technically optional, but only omit it
when the user explicitly asked for an empty/blank board or database. Never omit body as a
fallback because you could not load the authoring guidance — load it first via
getContentFormatGuide through the generic operation runner (execute) as
name=getContentFormatGuide, inputs={toolName} (createConfluencePage /
createConfluenceWhiteboard / createConfluenceDatabase), then build a real body.
A blank whiteboard
(no shapes, stickies, connectors, or layout) is almost never the intended result.
For doc types (page, live_doc, blogpost): format is html or markdown, value is the content string.
Prefer HTML. Use markdown only when you are confident the content needs only basic text
formatting and has no rich Confluence elements to create, such as panels, layouts, media,
whiteboard embeds, or Remixes. If unsure, use HTML.
For embed and smart_link: format must be url, value must be the URL to embed (e.g. https://example.com/design).
For whiteboard: format must be svg and value must be the complete initial SVG document with root width, height, and viewBox.
For database: format must be csv and value must be the complete initial CSV payload.
For a synced (Smart) Folder (contentType=folder): format must be url and value must be the
https URL of the external Google Drive, OneDrive, or SharePoint folder to sync from.
Requires the confluence_smart_folders_milestone_1 experiment; otherwise the create
returns FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED.
Do not pass patches, edit envelopes, or context on create.
Omit for a plain folder (no sync source) and for slide.

draft.description:
If true, create the content as a draft instead of publishing it. Only
supported when contentType is page or blogpost.

private.description:
If true, the created content is private to the caller: only the
creator has view and edit access. Supported for page, live_doc,
blogpost, whiteboard, database, and folder, including creation at the
homepage / sidebar root. Private creation is not supported for embed, smart_link, or slide.
This sets General access to VIEW_RESTRICTED and gives the creator one
Specific access grant, update (Can edit), which already includes
read/view. Do not add a separate read grant for the creator.
Omit or pass false for default visibility.

contentWidth.description:
Optional page width for doc types only: page, live_doc, and blogpost.
Omit unless the user explicitly requests a width; omission creates a
narrow page. Do not infer wide or max from body content or layout.
Accepted values are narrow, wide, and max.
Non-doc content types do not support this field.

tools.title: updateConfluenceContent
tools.description:
Update Confluence docs, whiteboards, or databases.
For edits to classic pages (type=page), fetch the full draft in the intended body format
with getConfluenceContent(draft=true, detail=full), and use that content and its returned snapshotToken.
If the token is missing, published-base or stale, refetch the draft and reapply the edit.
Update draft=true saves the draft; omit it to publish, according to user intent.

cloudId.description: Site UUID or Jira/Confluence URL for this operation's Atlassian site. cloudId is never silently auto-resolved or reused for you — call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE per session, cache the returned cloudId, and pass it explicitly on this and every subsequent call, since most operations need it. `execute` and its read/write/destructive variants strictly require it for cloudId-scoped operations and fail without it. Not needed for cloudId-less operations (e.g. Bitbucket), which ignore this field.

contentId.description: Numeric Confluence content ID. One of contentId or contentUrl is required.

contentUrl.description:
Full URL of the Confluence content. One of contentId or contentUrl is required.
Clear Confluence URLs for pages/live docs (/pages/{id}), blogs
(/blog/{id}), whiteboards (/whiteboard/{id}), databases
(/database/{id}), and folders (/folder/{id}) are normalized to their
numeric content ID before the update is sent, so URLs copied from the
product should work directly.

snapshotToken.description:
Opaque token from the most recent getConfluenceContent or updateConfluenceContent
response for this content. Each successful update returns the current snapshot.token;
pass it to the next update, because changes to the content make earlier tokens
stale. On snapshot_stale, re-read the content with getConfluenceContent and reapply
the change to the latest body before retrying; do not resend the same payload with
currentSnapshot.token.
Required for doc-type updates that mutate page/blog/live_doc content or contentWidth.
Not used for whiteboard svg or database csv object updates.

title.description: New title for the content. 1-255 characters. Omit to keep existing title.

body.description:
Before composing this body, follow the space-instruction decision rule in the tool
description. Reuse known instruction state and do not repeat the space lookup per write.
Body update object with format and value. Doc types accept format html or
markdown. Prefer HTML. Use markdown only when you are confident the content needs
only basic text formatting and has no rich Confluence elements to preserve or create,
such as panels, layouts, media, whiteboard embeds, or Remixes. If unsure, use HTML.
Re-read existing rich content as HTML before editing and preserve its content and embeds.
Whiteboards accept format svg and should include
context.content with the current SVG when applying a patch. Databases
accept format csv and should include context.content with the current
CSV when applying an edit envelope. Put the raw patch/envelope directly in
value; do not wrap it in an extra JSON object or {"content": "..."}
wrapper. For whiteboards, value is a patch, not a full SVG replacement.
For databases, value is an edit envelope, not a create payload. Mutually
exclusive with edits.

edits.description:
Granular edit operations. Array of tool-call objects, each with name
(replaceNode, insertNodeAfter, insertNodeBefore, deleteNode, removeNodes,
moveNode, appendNodeToEnd, setAttrs), localId, value, and arguments.
Mutually exclusive with body.

dryRun.description:
If true, validate and preview the result without persisting. For edits,
returns the resulting HTML. For body replacement, echoes the input.

draft.description:
If true, update the draft version instead of current. Only supported
for page and blogpost doc edits.

versionMessage.description: Optional version comment/message for the content update.

minorEdit.description: Whether to mark the new content version as a minor edit.

ownerId.description:
Atlassian account ID of the new owner to transfer page ownership to. Optional.
This is an account ID (e.g. 5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5), never an email/username
or a content ID. The new owner must already have edit permission.

contentWidth.description:
Optional page width for doc types only: page, live_doc, and blogpost.
Accepted values are narrow, wide, and max. The default width is narrow.
Omit to keep the existing content width unchanged.
A width-only update is valid and requires snapshotToken, but does not
require title, body, or edits.
Non-doc content types do not support this field.
